title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the notes 'Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques)' (1986), Grothendieck axiomatizes 1-dimensional 'formes' (connected 1-manifolds) combinatorially. The data are a set L of points and a set S of 'segments' I, each with a boundary ∂I of two points. The previous page fixes an orientation ω, so each segment has an origin or(I) and an end ex(I). It defines x ≺ y iff some segment I has x = or(I) and y = ex(I). It splits into the linear case (≺ transitive) and the circular case (≺ not transitive). This page treats the linear case.

(1) ≺ (written <) is a strict order. The endpoints of a segment are distinct, so x<y implies x≠y and < is irreflexive. Transitivity then gives asymmetry: x<y and y<x would give x<x.

(2) The segments are exactly the intervals [x,y] with x<y, and each has origin x for the chosen orientation. Hence the structure of a connected oriented 1-dimensional 'variété' is recovered from the order alone.

(3) The order satisfies the following conditions:
- strictly filtering upward: for all x,y there is z with x,y<z, so the order is directed and has no maximum;
- strictly filtering downward, dually;
- locally strictly filtering, in both directions. Upward version: if x≤y and x≤z, there is u≠x with x≤u≤y,z. This expresses that at each point there is a single right germ, and dually a single left germ, matching the 'germe de segment issu de x' of the previous page.

The left margin adds two things. It notes that in a more general 'variété' (probably one allowing branchings) only weaker filtering conditions hold. It also states, as I read it, a density condition: for x<y there is z with x<z<y.

The page ends by starting to prove upward strict filtration. The next page carries this out by induction on the length of a zigzag chain x_0 ≥ y_0 ≤ x_1 ≥ … coming from connectedness. That argument is the standard one: a connected poset in which any two elements over a common lower bound have a common upper bound is directed.

The aim is to show that the linear case is an unbounded dense total order (an 'open line' in order-theoretic form), and the circular case presumably a cyclic order. In other words, an order-theoretic or combinatorial characterization of connected 1-manifolds within a synthetic 'géométrie des formes'.
errors: No real error. The step 'x<y implies x≠y' depends on the axiom (doubted on the previous page) that the two points of ∂I are distinct; Grothendieck himself flags that it may need to be imposed as an axiom.
The local filtering condition as written ('x≤y,z ⇒ ∃u, x≤u≤y,z, u≠x') is only meaningful when y,z ≠ x; this hypothesis is implicit.
Totality of the order is not yet established on this page. Directedness is being proved, and totality would need the local uniqueness of germs plus connectedness.

ideas.what: Recovering an oriented connected 1-dimensional 'forme' (points + segments) from the strict order x<y iff x=or(I), y=ex(I); segments = closed intervals.
ideas.modern_name: Order-theoretic characterization of the line / interval structure of linearly ordered spaces (order topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cantor (dense countable orders), Veblen and Huntington (order axioms for the line), Hilbert (axioms of order)
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished 1986 notes; the general program of 'formes' and tame topology is announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984).

ideas.what: Linear vs circular dichotomy according to whether the segment relation is transitive.
ideas.modern_name: Linear orders vs cyclic orders; classification of connected 1-manifolds (line vs circle)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Huntington for cyclic orders; folklore classification of 1-manifolds)

ideas.what: Conditions 'strictement filtrante croissante/décroissante' and 'localement filtrante' (unique germ on each side), and density.
ideas.modern_name: Directed poset without endpoints; dense order; local linearity; 'no branching' condition

ideas.what: Marginal remark that in a more general 'variété' (with branchings) only weaker filtering conditions hold.
ideas.modern_name: Order-theoretic models of graphs/trees (R-trees, dendrites, branched 1-manifolds)

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out an elementary, classical step: the segments of an oriented 1-dimensional 'forme' induce a dense unbounded order that determines the structure. It is of historical interest as part of Grothendieck's synthetic 'géométrie des formes' (related to the tame-topology program of the Esquisse). But the mathematics is standard order theory and contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Line 'la structure de variété {+connexe [?]+} [-orientée-]': the inserted word above 'orientée' appears to read 'connexe' (or 'orientée' remains). The next words read 'de dim 1-forme' / 'de 1-forme', and the crossed word looks like 'régulière'.
The parenthetical in the local filtering condition should read 'et u ≠ x' rather than 'u ≠ dans z'.
Left margin, second note: likely 'i.e. quels que soient x<y distincts, ∃ z avec x<z<y' (density condition), written 'x<y, x<z<y' at the bottom.
Left margin, first note: likely 'dans une variété plus générale où il y a des points de ramification [?] … filtrante'. 'plans partout' is doubtful.
'Prenons p. ex. qu'elle est str. filtrante croissante' is probably 'Prouvons p. ex. qu'elle est str. filtrante croissante', since the next page gives the proof.
